title: slicer snapshot --json returns a dashboard's reads in one process, for one or several --root projects
findings_note: ork integration review 2026-10-19 (squalor-xyz/ork docs/review-2026-10-19-integration.md), R4: each slicer call costs about 0.4 s of Python startup under load; ork polls list, goals and relay-run list per project. Shape proposed in the report: chosen parts (items, goals, runs, held), several roots, a revision per part.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** `--if-changed` (an unchanged part printed without its value), a long-running `serve` mode (ork R9), a text form, and anything on ork's side.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork polls `list`, `goals` and `relay-run list` for every project it shows. Under the load of running relays, each slicer call costs 0.4 to 1.4 s, most of it Python startup (ork integration review 2026-10-19, R4, measured). One process for several projects measured about 0.08 s of CPU per project after startup (`list -r`, 17 projects). One `snapshot` call per refresh replaces three or more calls per project.

Owner decisions, 2026-10-19:

- A compact dashboard schema of slicer's own, not each command's output copied.
- A revision per part, so a reader can tell that a part has not changed.
- No `--if-changed` yet.

The schema is:

```
slicer snapshot --json [--root PATH]... [-r] [--parts items,goals,runs,status,health]

{"snapshot": 1, "slicer": VERSION, "contract": RELAY_CONTRACT,
 "projects": [{"root": ABS_PATH, "revision": REV,
   "parts": {
     "items":  {"revision": REV, "value": [{id, short_title, status, claim, pass, size, effort, score, quadrant, held, blocked}]},
     "goals":  {"revision": REV, "value": {goals: PROSE, non_goals: PROSE, records: [{id, kind, title}]}},
     "runs":   {"revision": REV, "value": [{id, items, worktree, state, updated_at, steps: [{id, role, phase, task, model}]}]},
     "status": {"revision": REV, "value": {next: ID or null, blocked: [ID], held: [ID]}},
     "health": {"revision": REV, "value": {render_stale: bool, merge_in_progress: bool}}},
   "error": null}]}
```

- `items` holds the items `list` shows by default (done and retired left out), in `list` order. `claim` is the claim owner or null. `held` means the item carries a configured hold flag. `blocked` means it waits on an unmet dependency.
- `runs` holds only active relay runs.
- `status.next` is what `next` would offer.
- A part's revision is the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of that part's `value` in canonical `jsonio` form. The project revision is the same hash taken over its part revisions in part order.
- A root that fails to load gets `parts: {}` and `error: {code, message, command}`, and the other roots still print, as with `-r`. The process exit is the highest exit of any project.
- The command is read-only and takes no lock.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/snapshot.py` (new): builds each part from a loaded `State`, reusing the readers `list`, `goals`, `status`, `relay-run list` and `check` already use (`cmd_list`, `cmd_goals`, `cmd_status` and `ops.next_item`, `relayrun.list_runs`, `check.run`, `vcs.merge_in_progress`), with no second copy of their rules.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `cmd_snapshot` and its parser. `--root` repeats here. `-r` reuses the walk behind `_recursive_flag` and `_recursive`.
- `tests/test_snapshot.py` (new).
- `docs/commands.md` (a `snapshot` row), `docs/agents.md` (its JSON contract, next to the `-r` section), `CHANGELOG.md` under Added.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Snapshot_OneRoot_CarriesEveryPartInOrder`: the top-level keys are `snapshot`, `slicer`, `contract` and `projects`, and the part keys are `items`, `goals`, `runs`, `status`, `health`, in that order. `slicer` is `__version__` and `contract` is `ai.RELAY_CONTRACT`.
- `test_Snapshot_ItemsRow_MatchesListOrderAndFields`: the rows follow `list`'s default order and carry the eleven fields. A held item and a blocked item are marked.
- `test_Snapshot_RepeatedRoot_OneProjectEachInGivenOrder`: two `--root` values give two projects, in the order given, each with an absolute `root`.
- `test_Snapshot_Recursive_FindsNestedProjects`: `-r` lists the nested projects in sorted path order, as `list -r` does.
- `test_Snapshot_Parts_OnlyNamedParts`: `--parts items,health` prints only those two. An unknown part name is `usage` and prints nothing.
- `test_Snapshot_Revision_ChangesOnlyWithItsPart`: after `set` on one item, the `items` revision and the project revision change, and the `goals` revision does not. Two runs with no change in between print the same bytes.
- `test_Snapshot_BadRoot_ReportsErrorAndOthersPrint`: a missing root has `parts: {}` and an `error` with a code, the good root still prints, and the exit is that error's exit.
- `test_Snapshot_Health_ReportsRenderStaleAndMerge`: a stale render sets `render_stale`, and a merge in progress in a fixture repo sets `merge_in_progress`.
- `test_Snapshot_Runs_OnlyActive`: an ended run is left out.
- `test_Snapshot_WithoutJson_IsUsage`.
- `test_Snapshot_WhileLocked_StillReadsAndWritesNothing`: it works while another process holds the project lock, and the index bytes do not change.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. Build each part from the existing readers, then the revisions, then the envelope and the walk over roots.
3. Document the command and its JSON contract. Add a CHANGELOG entry.
4. Mutation-check each new test. Every fixture that needs git is its own repo or uses `support.isolated_discovery`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes. `slicer snapshot --json --root .` parses.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
